title: Artefact unveils AI sovereignty framework as UAE moves half of government services to Agentic AI
summary: The white paper was written to support the agentic AI transformation objectives of the Abu Dhabi Government and the UAE federal government Artefact presented the paper in Abu Dhabi to senior government officials and business leaders, with an address by H.E. Marie Audouard, Ambassador of France to the UAE Exclusive dinner brought together senior public- and private-sector leaders for discussions on AI adoption and government agentification Abu Dhabi, UAE - Artefact, a global leader in AI deployment, has published ‘Closing the AI Sovereignty Gap,’ a white paper that sets out how UAE government entities can scale agentic AI while keeping control of the infrastructure, data, models and agents behind it. The paper was unveiled at an exclusive Artefact AI Connect Dinner in Abu Dhabi, bringing together senior government officials, business executives and industry leaders from the public and private sectors. The evening provided a platform to exchange perspectives on the opportunities and challenges of scaling AI adoption across the UAE, with a focus on the role of strategic partnerships in supporting AI implementation across government entities and businesses. H.E. Marie Audouard, Ambassador of France to the UAE, opened the evening with an address highlighting the strong ties between France and the UAE and the opportunities to further strengthen bilateral cooperation through joint initiatives in artificial intelligence and innovation. She said: “Artificial intelligence has become a strategic pillar of the France-UAE partnership, reflecting the shared ambition and determination of both countries to work together. Artefact’s presence in the UAE, as evidenced by its recent recognition as Google Cloud’s AI Partner of the Year for EMEA, illustrates the growing role of French expertise in AI, data, and digital transformation.” The gathering featured insights from Vincent Luciani, Co-founder and Executive Chairman of Artefact, who shared perspectives on how organizations can move beyond isolated AI applications to reinvent core operations, emphasizing AI sovereignty, responsible governance and human-centric transformation as drivers of competitive advantage. Christelle Salame, Managing Partner at Artefact examined the agentification of government processes and services, its potential to transform interactions with citizens, residents and businesses, and the key opportunities and challenges surrounding its implementation.
